description: Backend: Notification model, FCM/notification services, notification API routes, event hooks in existing controllers, User model additions. This is the foundation all other features depend on.
steps: Step 1 — Install firebase-admin: In the workspace root, run `npm install firebase-admin`. This adds the Firebase Admin SDK to package.json and node_modules.

Step 2 — Extend models/User.js: Add two new fields to userSchema before the closing brace of the schema definition: `fcmToken: { type: String, default: null }` and `notificationsEnabled: { type: Boolean, default: true }`. These are the only changes to User.js.

Step 3 — Create models/Notification.js: New Mongoose model with ES module export. Schema fields: user (ObjectId ref User, required, indexed), type (String, enum: ['order','security','product','promo','account'], required), title (String, required), message (String, required), entityId (String, default null — order._id, product._id, etc.), entityType (String, enum: ['order','product','promo','user',null], default null), isRead (Boolean, default false, indexed), metadata (Object, default {}), createdAt (Date, default Date.now, indexed). Add a compound index on {user:1, createdAt:-1} for efficient pagination. Export as `mongoose.models.Notification || mongoose.model('Notification', notificationSchema)`.

Step 4 — Create services/fcmService.js: ES module. Initialize Firebase Admin lazily (only once, guarded by admin.apps.length check). Read credentials from process.env.FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY (a JSON string) and process.env.FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID. Export async function `sendPushNotification(fcmToken, title, body, data={})` that calls `admin.messaging().send({token, notification:{title,body}, data, android:{priority:'high'}})`. Catches and logs errors; returns {success:boolean, messageId?}. Also export `sendMulticastNotification(tokens[], title, body, data={})` using `admin.messaging().sendEachForMulticast`. If FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID or FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY is not set, log a warning and return {success:false, reason:'FCM not configured'} rather than throwing.

Step 5 — Create services/notificationService.js: ES module. Import Notification model and fcmService. Export the following functions:
  - `createNotification(userId, type, title, message, entityId=null, entityType=null, metadata={})`: saves a Notification document and returns it.
  - `notifyOrderUpdate(order, status)`: called after order status changes. Looks up the order.user to get their fcmToken and notificationsEnabled. Maps status to a human-readable title+message (e.g. 'confirmed' → 'Order Confirmed', 'Your order #XXXXXXX has been confirmed.'). Calls createNotification then sendPushNotification if the user has a token and notificationsEnabled===true. entityId=order._id.toString(), entityType='order'.
  - `notifyOrderPlaced(order, userId)`: for newly created orders. title='Order Placed', message='Your order #<orderId> has been received.'.
  - `notifyPaymentSuccess(order, userId)`: title='Payment Successful', message='Payment for order #<orderId> confirmed.'.
  - `notifyPaymentFailed(order, userId)`: title='Payment Failed', message='Payment for order #<orderId> could not be processed.'.
  - `notifyNewProduct(product)`: fetches all users where notificationsEnabled===true and fcmToken != null. Calls createNotification for each user, then sendMulticastNotification with all tokens. entityId=product._id.toString(), entityType='product'. title='New Product Available', message='<product.name> is now available in <product.category>.'.
  - `notifyPromoApplied(userId, promoCode, discountAmount, orderId)`: title='Promo Code Applied', message='Code "<promoCode>" saved you $<discountAmount> on order #<orderId>.'.
  - `notifySecurityEvent(userId, eventType)`: eventType in ['new_login','password_changed']. Maps to appropriate title/message. Does NOT send push notifications for security events — saves DB record only (security alerts must always reach the notification center regardless of push preference).
  - `notifyProfileUpdated(userId)`: title='Profile Updated', message='Your profile information was successfully updated.'
  All functions are non-blocking for the calling HTTP request — use setImmediate or fire-and-forget pattern with a .catch(console.error) so a notification failure never crashes an order route.

Step 6 — Create routes/notifications.js: Express router, ES module. All routes require protectRoute middleware. Routes:
  GET /                → paginated list for req.user._id, query params: page(default 1), limit(default 20). Returns {success, data:[notifications], unreadCount, totalPages}.
  GET /unread-count    → {success, count: Number} — count of isRead:false for req.user.
  PATCH /:id/read      → mark one notification as read (verify ownership: notification.user must equal req.user._id).
  PATCH /read-all      → mark all of req.user's notifications as read.
  DELETE /:id          → delete one notification (verify ownership).
  PATCH /preferences   → update req.user's fcmToken and/or notificationsEnabled. Body: {fcmToken?, notificationsEnabled?}. Uses User.findByIdAndUpdate. Returns {success, user: updated}.
  GET /preferences     → return {success, fcmToken: masked, notificationsEnabled} for current user.
  All routes return JSON. Follow the existing pattern: try/catch, 200/201/400/404/500 status codes consistent with other routes.

Step 7 — Mount the new route in server.js: Add `import notificationRoutes from './routes/notifications.js'` at the top (with the other imports), then add `app.use('/api/notifications', notificationRoutes)` after the existing app.use lines, before the 404 catch-all.

Step 8 — Hook notifyOrderPlaced into controller/orders.js createOrder: After `await Order.create(req.body)` succeeds (line ~47), add a non-blocking call: `setImmediate(async () => { try { const { notifyOrderPlaced } = await import('../services/notificationService.js'); await notifyOrderPlaced(order, req.user?._id); } catch(e){ console.error('[notify]', e); } });`. Import is dynamic to avoid circular dependencies.

Step 9 — Hook notifyOrderUpdate into controller/orders.js updateOrderStatus: After `await order.save()` succeeds (line ~154 in the original), add: `setImmediate(async () => { try { const { notifyOrderUpdate } = await import('../services/notificationService.js'); await notifyOrderUpdate(order, status); } catch(e){ console.error('[notify]', e); } });`. This covers all status transitions from the dashboard: confirmed, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled, etc.

Step 10 — Hook notifyPaymentSuccess and notifyPaymentFailed into routes/stripe.js: In the `confirm-payment` handler, after the `updatedOrder` is saved (after `await incrementSoldCount(updatedOrder)`), add a setImmediate block calling `notifyPaymentSuccess(updatedOrder, req.user._id)`. In the webhook `payment_intent.payment_failed` handler, after the DB update, add `notifyPaymentFailed(updated, updated?.user)`. In the webhook `payment_intent.succeeded` handler, after `await incrementSoldCount(updated)`, add `notifyPaymentSuccess(updated, updated?.user)`.

Step 11 — Hook notifyNewProduct into controller/product.js createProduct: After `await product.save()` succeeds, add a setImmediate block calling `notifyNewProduct(product)`. This fires only when a genuine new product is created through the dashboard.

Step 12 — Hook notifyPromoApplied into controller/orders.js createOrder: Inside the existing `if (req.body.promoCode && req.user?._id)` block that already calls recordRedemption, add to the same setImmediate call: `notifyPromoApplied(req.user._id, req.body.promoCode, req.body.discountAmount || 0, order.orderId)`.

Step 13 — Hook notifySecurityEvent into controller/user.js: In the Login function, after the JWT is created and before the return (line ~37 area), add: `setImmediate(async () => { try { const { notifySecurityEvent } = await import('../services/notificationService.js'); await notifySecurityEvent(user._id, 'new_login'); } catch(e){} });`. In the changePassword function, after `await user.save()`, add the same pattern with eventType 'password_changed'.

Step 14 — Create .env additions documentation: Add a comment block at the top of the existing .env file (do NOT expose actual values) noting the two new required variables: `# FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY=<paste entire service account JSON as a single line, or set path>` and `# FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=your-project-id`. This is documentation only.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/notifications returns an empty array for a new user (not a 500 error).
After a test order is created via POST /api/orders, a Notification document with type='order' appears in MongoDB for that user.
PATCH /api/notifications/preferences with body {notificationsEnabled:false} updates the User document in MongoDB.
If FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY is not set in .env, the server starts without crashing and notificationService logs a warning.
After admin changes an order status via PUT /api/orders/:id, a new Notification document appears for that order's user.
After createProduct is called, Notification documents are created for users with notificationsEnabled:true.
verification: Start the backend: `node server.js` — confirm no startup errors in console.
Authenticate: POST /api/auth/login, capture the JWT token.
GET /api/notifications with Authorization: Bearer <token> — expect 200 with {success:true, data:[], unreadCount:0}.
PATCH /api/notifications/preferences with body {notificationsEnabled:false} — expect 200, then verify in MongoDB: db.users.findOne({email:'...'}).notificationsEnabled === false.
Create an order via POST /api/orders, then query db.notifications.find({user: <userId>}) — expect at least one document with type='order'.
PUT /api/orders/:id with body {status:'confirmed'} — expect a new notification in db.notifications for that order's user.
Confirm `node server.js` still starts cleanly with no FCM key set (warning only, no crash).
findings: API response shapes: GET /api/notifications → {success:true, data:[{_id,user,type,title,message,entityId,entityType,isRead,metadata,createdAt}], unreadCount:Number, totalPages:Number, currentPage:Number}. GET /api/notifications/unread-count → {success:true, count:Number}. PATCH /api/notifications/:id/read → {success:true, data:{notification}}. PATCH /api/notifications/read-all → {success:true, message:String}. DELETE /api/notifications/:id → {success:true, data:{}}. PATCH /api/notifications/preferences → {success:true, user:{...userDoc without password}}. GET /api/notifications/preferences → {success:true, fcmToken:maskedString|null, notificationsEnabled:Boolean}. Env vars needed: FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY (full service-account JSON as single-line string) and FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID. FCM is lazy-initialized — server starts cleanly without these vars set (logs warning only when a push is attempted). firebase-admin installed at exact version present in package-lock.json. Notification types enum: ['order','security','product','promo','account']. EntityType enum: ['order','product','promo','user',null]. Security notifications (new_login, password_changed) are DB-only, no push. All notification hooks use setImmediate fire-and-forget with .catch(console.error) so failures never crash request handlers.
